topic: GC-side recovered-in-degree warning was often a false alarm caused by a dedup-ad
canonical_claim: The GC-side recovered-in-degree warning was often a false alarm caused by a dedup-adopt-versus-condemn TOCTOU: a writer adopted a blob after GC read it as not condemned, and GC then spared it after recovering the fresh edge.; The dedup-adoption condemnation check remains safety-critical because adoption does not mutate the existing incarnation and a graduated delete can race an adoption that was not checked. Additionally, The K1 dedup-adoption gate is safety-critical: adopting an existing incarnation is invisible to GC's in-flight delete decision, so a condemned adopted blob must be displaced with a fresh incarnation.

topic: Advancing the janitor cursor from page `A` to `B` during a suppressed DEFER can
canonical_claim: Advancing the janitor cursor from page `A` to `B` during a suppressed DEFER can form the fair `A-defer -> B-fold -> A` cycle, permanently skipping page `A` and violating `EventuallyDeadAReclaimed`.; A valid janitor page under destructive suppression does not advance its cursor, preventing alternating `DEFER` and fold rounds from permanently skipping a dead page.

topic: Removing the `deferCount < MaxDefer` guard permits a fair infinite DEFER sequenc
canonical_claim: Removing the `deferCount < MaxDefer` guard permits a fair infinite DEFER sequence in which nonempty `unfolded` deltas are never folded, violating `EventuallyFolded`.; DEFER leaves the sealed `(snap_generation, snap_attempt)` unchanged, so journals accumulate naturally from the old sealed cursor and a later FOLD processes the accumulated deltas without new persisted accumulator state. Additionally, The pre-fold DEFER decision uses only O(shards) `LIST(cas/refs/)` token-diff signals, O(retired-entries + servers) graduation-due signals, and an O(1) defer window; it does not read journals or inspect whether a changed shard contains `+1` or `−1` content. Additionally, `gc_fold_max_defer_rounds` bounds batching so every accumulated delta is folded within a bounded number of rounds; a due destructive decision also forces a FOLD. Additionally, A deferred GC round reports `RoundReport::deferred=true`, emits a round event with `outcome = "deferred"`, and leaves the sealed generation pinned without fold, delete, or round-commit CAS; a FOLD resets the leader-local defer counter. Additionally, Phase 4 Lever A lets a GC round re-adopt the sealed in-degree generation as DEFER when cheap pre-fold signals show no destructive decision; due graduation forces a fold, and the safety gate is `CaGcRoundDeferCore`.

topic: Graduating a blob without first checking that `unfolded` contains no pending del
canonical_claim: Graduating a blob without first checking that `unfolded` contains no pending delta for that blob can physically delete it after a protective `+1` lands after the fold cut, violating `NoOverDelete`.; The delete guard in `GComplete` must force a fold for any pending delta touching the candidate blob, and `unfolded` carries both `add` and `del` signs.

topic: destructive gate based only on `proven == total` accepts an empty universe becau
canonical_claim: A destructive gate based only on `proven == total` accepts an empty universe because `0 == 0`; the gate therefore needs an explicit nonempty-authority predicate.; A classification-4 `ShardCoverage` hold stores a bounded reason, offending position, and retry/backoff data per `(namespace, incarnation)`; `suppress_destructive = anomalies || carried_holds || !frontier_complete` is recomputed before every destructive site. Additionally, `suppress_destructive` is true when anomalies exist, a hold is carried, or the frontier is incomplete, and it must be consulted at every destructive site including manifest deletion, generation prune, orphan sweep, handoff reclaim, and ref cleanup. Additionally, The destructive gate remains `suppress_destructive = anomalies || carried_holds || !frontier_complete`; the Stage B change permits `frontier_complete` to become true from catalog proof but does not weaken any suppression term. Additionally, Destructive GC is permitted only when `frontier_complete = true` and `suppress_destructive = false`; the suppression gate remains `anomalies || carried_holds || !frontier_complete`. Additionally, The destructive gate formula is `frontier_complete = universe_authoritative && frontier_namespaces > 0 && frontier_proven == frontier_namespaces` and `suppress_destructive = anomalies || carried_holds || !frontier_complete`. Additionally, The destructive gate has five independent suppressors: non-empty anomalies, non-empty carried holds, `!universe_authoritative`, `frontier_namespaces == 0`, and `frontier_proven != frontier_namespaces`. Additionally, The destructive frontier gate is complete only when `universe_authoritative` is true, `result.frontier_namespaces > 0`, and `result.frontier_proven == result.frontier_namespaces`; anomalies, carried holds, or any incomplete frontier suppress destructive work. Additionally, The physical GC destructive gate is open only when the universe is authoritative, the frontier namespace count is nonzero, the proven frontier equals the namespace universe, and neither anomalies nor carried holds suppress destruction. Additionally, When the frontier is not complete, destructive work is suppressed pool-wide because blob in-degree is pool-wide and there is no ownership partition of the blob space. Additionally, `suppress_destructive` is computed as `!report.anomalies.empty() || !carried_holds.empty() || frontier_incomplete`; the authoritative flip changes only the value of `universe_authoritative` in the `frontier_complete` expression. Additionally, An authoritative empty universe is not a complete frontier: `frontier_namespaces > 0` is required so `0 == 0` cannot open destructive work. Additionally, The production destructive gate is complete only when `universe_authoritative` is true, `frontier_namespaces > 0`, and `frontier_proven == frontier_namespaces`; `suppress_destructive` is then `!report.anomalies.empty() || !carried_holds.empty() || frontier_incomplete`. Additionally, At the destructive gate call site, `!suppress_destructive` implies `frontier_complete`, which implies `universe_authoritative`; therefore `planManifestCursorPage` receives an authoritative recovery argument whenever the gate opens.

topic: single incomplete GC `LIST` page can permanently skip a durable receiver `+1`
canonical_claim: A single incomplete GC `LIST` page can permanently skip a durable receiver `+1`: the namespace cursor advances past the omitted transaction, the sender `-1` folds, and a deduplicated blob reaches physical deletion while a promoted manifest still references it.

topic: stale in-degree edges
canonical_claim: A `stale_edge` is a blob whose every source edge names a manifest that no longer exists; its positive in-degree is pinned forever, so incremental GC cannot reclaim it and only `ca-gc-rebuild` or an in-degree rebuild can clear the condition. One fsck report identified 12 unreferenced objects with exactly this condition.; The fsck `stale_edge` class is detail-mode only and should be emitted when every in-degree edge for a blob names an absent manifest; a blob remains ordinary `AwaitingGc` when any edge still names a present manifest.

topic: precommit that records its blob closure lazily from a tree object can record an
canonical_claim: A precommit that records its blob closure lazily from a tree object can record an empty closure after the tree disappears, causing a blob to leak forever.

topic: deposed leader's pre-CAS `clearSparedMeta` could leave stray `Clean` metadata ov
canonical_claim: A deposed leader's pre-CAS `clearSparedMeta` could leave stray `Clean` metadata over a `delete_pending` blob, allowing a writer to reuse the condemned exact token and a pending exact-token redelete to delete the live reuse; add-only GC freshness metadata fixed this INV_NO_LOSS risk.; A pre-release v3 data-loss hole was found while modeling the deposed-leader path in TLA+: a deposed GC leader's pre-CAS `clearSparedMeta` call leaves stray-Clean freshness metadata over a `delete_pending` blob; a writer can then reuse the condemned blob's exact token, and the pending exact-token redelete for that token deletes the live reuse, violating `INV_NO_LOSS`. The fix made GC freshness metadata add-only (never `Condemned`->`Clean` on a spare leader; only a writer holding a fresh incarnation token may publish `Clean`), verified by a TLA+ witness plus 5 sabotage configurations including a `post_adoption_clear` case that produces an authentic 16-state 2-leader counterexample against the naive fix.; `clearSparedMeta` (`Core/CasGc.cpp:106-113`) clears a blob's freshness meta from Condemned to Clean when a GC round spares it, scheduled on the spare verdict and completed BEFORE the round's single `gc/state` CAS; a GC leader that runs it and then loses the CAS leaves a durable stray-Clean meta over a blob still `delete_pending` in the durably-adopted run. Stray-Clean is the unsafe direction (unlike stray-Condemned, which only costs an unnecessary resurrect) because it defeats the writer's freshness gate, letting a writer reuse the exact condemned incarnation token; a later pending exact-token redelete then deletes the live reused incarnation.; A fresh GC leader's spare is add-only and cannot cancel a stale leader's already-captured pre-CAS delete.

topic: GC discovery no longer performs the roots-tree quadratic
canonical_claim: GC discovery no longer performs the roots-tree quadratic: it lists flat `cas/refs/` and uses streamed pagination with `start_after=cursor`.; GC discovery enumerates the live root-shard universe with `LIST(cas/refs/)`, and this LIST sweep is the only universe-proportional operation in a regular round.; GC performs one paginated global `LIST cas/refs/` per round for ref intake, snapshot observation, and cleanup planning; it does not perform per-table LISTs or snapshot HEADs. Additionally, `GC` performs one global paginated `LIST cas/refs/` with explicit start-after resume and persists per-table `last_folded_ref_id` cursors in the existing fold artifacts through the existing single `gc/state` CAS.

topic: manifest cleanup budget durability
canonical_claim: The manifest-cleanup GC phase is a one-shot pipeline: its `-1` edge is consumed in the same CAS that produces `mf_cleanup`, so a per-round cap can permanently skip entries rather than defer them to the next intake.; The one-shot `manifest_deletes` pipeline consumes owner-removal edges in the same CAS that creates `folded.mf_cleanup` before deletion, so a cap-declined entry is not re-derived and an orphan-manifest sweep of about 100 objects per round cannot keep pace.; The one-shot `gc_round_manifest_cleanup_budget` cap was unsafe: the ref-log cursor could consume an owner-removal entry in the same CAS as a cap-declined cleanup, making the manifest permanently unreachable; durable retry is required before bounding this work.; When `gc_round_manifest_cleanup_budget` is exhausted, manifest bodies nominated but declined in that round are not re-derived by later rounds, creating an unbounded unreachable-manifest leak.

topic: Stage A residual missing-universe case is unsafe
canonical_claim: The Stage A residual missing-universe case is unsafe: an acknowledged hidden A:+1 in a namespace absent from both the hint and gc/state can coexist with visible B:-1, allowing the shared blob to reach zero and be deleted while A still owns it; Under the Stage A default, a namespace absent from both the hint and `gc/state` can hold an acknowledged shared-blob `+1` while another namespace exposes a `-1`, yet the required result is zero deletes because `StageA_Suppressed` prevents data loss. Additionally, Production destruction was suppressed in Stage A because pool-wide blob in-degree could contain an acknowledged `+1` from an invisible namespace while a visible `-1` was folded; suppression may be lifted only after the namespace universe is authoritative.
